newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Ericsson, Nokia in record territory.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Ericsson, Nokia in record territory.

text.p: Nordic telecommunications equipment suppliers Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson and Nokia Group rose to 12-month highs Wednesday to stand out among American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Traders said European ADRs were benefiting from a stronger dollar that was helping boost the profit margins of big exporting companies.
"A lot of the perception is that (Europe) is the place to be," a trader said. "... All these companies that are dollar-driven are making a lot more money now."
Ericsson rose 1-10/16 to 42-5/16 in mid-morning trade of 1.6 million shares that put the ADRs on the Nasdaq's most-active list. Nokia was up 2-5/16 to 82.
Traders said Ericsson and Nokia were being pulled higher by rival Motorola Inc's above-forecast second-quarter earnings.
Among other European ADRS, Anglo-Dutch conglomerate Unilever NV rose 1-1/4 to 225-1/2, close to a 12-month high. Dutch software company Baan Co NV was up 1-15/16 to a 12-month record of 78-5/16.
British news and information company Reuters Holdings fell 2-15/16 amid speculation the strength of sterling could lead to further cuts in earnings projections.

Among Latin American ADRs, Telefonos de Mexico rose 1/8 to 52-7/8. Brazilian telephone holding the government announced a consortium headed by BellSouth Corp of the United States had won a 20-year concession to run private cellular telephone services in Sao Paulo.
The 814-strong ADR group was up 0.07 percent in late morning. ADRs allow U.S. trade of foreign shares.
